An elderly man, aged 88, is discovered on his kitchen floor and transported to the Emergency
Department by EMS after neighbors alerted police of his absence. He has no notable medical history.
The patient is found to be lethargic but can be aroused, and is unable to explain how he ended up on
the floor. His vital signs show significant postural hypotension, with supine blood pressure of 123/82
mm Hg dropping to 70/40 mm Hg upon raising the head of the bed. Physical examination reveals
Kussmaul breathing pattern with clear lungs, normal cardiovascular findings, and no neurological
deficits. Laboratory findings are as follows: Serum: Na+ 132 mEq/L Cl− 114 mEq/L K+ 2.8 mEq/L
HCO3− 6 mEq/L Urea nitrogen 52 mg/dL Creatinine 2.8 mg/dL Arterial Blood Gas: pH 7.23 PCO2 19
mm Hg HCO3 6 mEq/L Based on these findings, what is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices:
(A) Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis and respiratory acidosis (B) Triple acid-base disorder:
metabolic acidosis, respiratory acidosis, and metabolic alkalosis (C) Mixed metabolic acidosis with
appropriate respiratory compensation (D) Metabolic alkalosis (E) High anion gap metabolic acidosis

and respiratory alkalosis (F) High anion gap metabolic acidosis (G) Combined metabolic and
respiratory acidosis with hypokalemia (H) Mixed high and normal anion gap metabolic acidosis (I)
Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis (J) Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with incomplete
respiratory compensation
 A. Metabolic alkalosis
B. High anion gap metabolic acidosis
C. Combined metabolic and respiratory acidosis with hypokalemia
D. Mixed high and normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
E. Mixed metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
F. Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
G. Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with incomplete respiratory compensation
H. Triple acid-base disorder: metabolic acidosis, respiratory acidosis, and metabolic alkalosis
I. High anion gap metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis
J. Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis and respiratory acidosis
